question.prompt:
Given \(AB\parallel CD\), point \(E\) lies between them, \(\angle B=30^\circ\), and \(\angle D=40^\circ\). Find \(\angle BED\). (Here \(\angle B\) denotes \(\angle ABE\), and \(\angle D\) denotes \(\angle CDE\); points \(A\), \(C\), and \(E\) lie on the same side of line \(BD\); unit: degrees; enter only the numerical value.)

[Figure 1](figures/cnm_070_q1_question_en.svg)

solutions.explanation: Through point \(E\), draw \(EF\parallel AB\). Then \(EF\parallel CD\), \(\angle BEF=\angle B=30^\circ\), and \(\angle DEF=\angle D=40^\circ\), so \(\angle BED=30^\circ+40^\circ=70^\circ\).
solutions.title: Draw a parallel through E

solutions.explanation:
Triangle \(BDE\) gives the required angle once we find the sum of its other two angles. Let \(\alpha=\angle ABD\) and \(\beta=\angle CDB\). Since \(AB\parallel CD\), these same-side interior angles satisfy \(\alpha+\beta=180^\circ\). The stated position of \(E\) means \(BE\) splits \(\angle ABD\) and \(DE\) splits \(\angle CDB\). Therefore,
\[
\angle EBD+\angle BDE=(\alpha-30^\circ)+(\beta-40^\circ)=110^\circ.
\]
The angles of triangle \(BDE\) sum to \(180^\circ\), so \(\angle BED=180^\circ-110^\circ=70^\circ\).
solutions.title: Use triangle BDE
